title: Long-Term Care Institution Designation in Korea: Requirements and Procedure | YouSun Administrative Agency
h1: Long-Term Care Institution Designation in Korea
lead: To run a long-term care institution in Korea that provides in-home benefits such as home-visit care or day/night care, or facility benefits, you must have the facilities and staff set by Ministry of Health and Welfare ordinance and be designated by the competent head of the si/gun/gu. An in-home elderly welfare facility must first file an installation report, and the designation is valid for 6 years.
summary: Scope: long-term care institutions providing in-home benefits (home-visit care, home-visit bathing, home-visit nursing, day/night care, short-term care, etc.) or facility benefits.
Filed with: the Mayor of the Special Self-Governing City, the Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or the head of the si/gun/gu with jurisdiction (reviewed by a designation review committee).
Key requirements: meet the facility and staffing standards (for in-home care, the standards of the Enforcement Rule of the Welfare of Older Persons Act), and no disqualification.
Fee: confirm the designation application fee with the competent si/gun/gu office.
Processing: 30 days according to the application form; designation valid for 6 years (apply for renewal at least 90 days before expiry).

sections.h2: Who must obtain long-term care institution designation?
sections.body: Under the Long-Term Care Insurance for Older Persons Act, a person who intends to run a long-term care institution providing in-home or facility benefits must have the facilities and staff and be designated by the head of the si/gun/gu with jurisdiction over the location. Facilities eligible for designation are elderly medical welfare facilities and in-home elderly welfare facilities under the Welfare of Older Persons Act. Running a long-term care institution without designation is subject to criminal penalties.

(1) Facilities and staff (in-home benefits): the standards of the Enforcement Rule of the Welfare of Older Persons Act apply. Facilities for home-visit care, home-visit bathing and home-visit nursing need a dedicated floor area of 16.5 square metres or more, plus an office and equipment needed for the business such as communication equipment and furniture; home-visit bathing also needs a portable bathtub or a mobile bathing vehicle, and home-visit nursing needs items such as a blood-pressure monitor and thermometer. Day/night care and short-term care facilities need a total floor area of 90 square metres or more (with an additional 6.6 square metres or more per person if the capacity is 6 or more).

(2) Qualifications of the facility head and staff: the head of a home-visit care facility, for example, must be a social worker, a medical professional, or a person with a certain period of work experience who has completed prescribed training.

(3) Matters reviewed: designation considers the operator's history of providing long-term care benefits, administrative sanctions, the operating plan, and the local elderly population and demand for long-term care benefits.

(4) Disqualifications: minors, adults under full or limited guardianship, persons with mental illness (except those a specialist finds suitable), persons addicted to narcotics, bankrupts who have not been reinstated, persons for whom 5 years have not passed since serving a sentence of imprisonment without labour or heavier, persons serving a suspended sentence, and corporations whose representative falls under any of these cannot be designated.

Submit the long-term care institution designation application with the general status, staffing status and facility status, a copy of the business registration certificate or unique number certificate (can be checked through shared administrative information), and the business plan and operating rules. An in-home elderly welfare facility must first file an installation report (with the head of the si/gun/gu) under the Welfare of Older Persons Act, and the documents for that report follow the Act's Enforcement Rule. Additional documents may apply depending on the facility type, so confirm finally with the elderly welfare department of the competent si/gun/gu.

(1) Decide the service type → (2) file the in-home elderly welfare facility installation report and secure facilities and staff → (3) optional prior consultation on designation standards with the competent si/gun/gu → (4) submit the designation application and documents → (5) review by the long-term care institution designation review committee → (6) designation decision and issuance of the designation certificate (if refused, reasons are given in writing) → (7) the designation details are notified to the National Health Insurance Service.

The processing period on the application form is 30 days. Time for securing facilities, filing the installation report and hiring staff is separate, and the composition and operation of the review committee are determined by the local government. The designation is valid for 6 years, and to keep it you must apply for renewal at least 90 days before it expires.

Apply to the Mayor of the Special Self-Governing City, the Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or the head of the si/gun/gu with jurisdiction over the location. For home-visit nursing operated by a person who is not a medical institution, a nurse must be appointed as the manager in charge.

sections.h2: What are the statutory fees for designation?
sections.body: The designation application fee should be confirmed with the competent authority (the si/gun/gu office).

sections.h2: Why is designation refused or revoked?
sections.body: Facility or staffing standards not met, a disqualification, an incomplete operating plan, or past administrative sanctions can be issues. After designation, obtaining it by false or fraudulent means, ceasing to meet the designation standards, or providing services outside the benefits, among others, are grounds for revocation of designation or business suspension of up to 6 months. Running a long-term care institution without designation or obtaining designation by fraudulent means can lead to imprisonment of up to 2 years or a fine of up to KRW 20 million.

sections.h2: What can an administrative agent help with?
sections.body: YouSun Administrative Agency prepares documents such as the installation report, designation application, business plan and operating rules, reviews requirements and submits them to the authority on your authorization. Care-worker training, benefit claims and evaluation responses, and facility construction are not handled. Work restricted by other laws cannot be handled, and litigation or court representation is outside the scope of an administrative agent and is not offered. Whether designation is granted is decided by the competent authority.

faq.q: Is a long-term care institution licensed or designated?
faq.a: Designated. You must have the facilities and staff and be designated by the head of the si/gun/gu with jurisdiction.

faq.q: Is an installation report for an in-home elderly welfare facility needed first?
faq.a: Yes. A person other than the State or a local government who intends to install an in-home elderly welfare facility must report to the head of the si/gun/gu, who must accept the report if it complies with the Act.

faq.q: What floor area does a home-visit care centre need?
faq.a: A dedicated floor area of 16.5 square metres or more (based on floor area), with an office and equipment such as communication equipment and furniture.

faq.q: What is the floor-area standard for a day/night care centre?
faq.a: A total floor area of 90 square metres or more; if the capacity is 6 or more, an additional living room or bedroom space of 6.6 square metres or more per person must be secured.

faq.q: How long is the designation valid?
faq.a: 6 years from the date of designation. To renew, apply at least 90 days before it expires.

faq.q: Does the designation lapse if the renewal review is delayed?
faq.a: If renewal is not completed within the validity period, the designation is deemed valid until the review decision is made.

faq.q: How do I close or suspend the institution?
faq.a: Closure or suspension must be reported as required by law, and not providing long-term care benefits for 1 year or more without reporting is a ground for revoking the designation.
